metadata.title: Developer terms | Boardsesh for developers
metadata.description: The terms an app accepts when it registers to connect to Boardsesh accounts.

terms.title: Boardsesh developer terms
terms.intro: These terms apply to anyone who registers an app that connects to Boardsesh accounts through the Boardsesh API. You accept them when you register an app, for yourself and for everyone who works on the app with you.

items.purpose: Use what a climber shares only for the features they connected your app for.
items.noSale: Don’t sell or rent it, and don’t share it with anyone for advertising, profiling or data brokering.
items.setterClimbs: A tick comes with the climb it is on, including a draft or an unlisted climb someone else set. That detail is there so the climber can see their own logbook. Don’t publish it, show it to other people or build a list of climbs from it.
items.delete: Delete a climber’s Boardsesh data when they disconnect your app or ask you to, unless they ask you to keep it.
items.privacyPolicy: Have a privacy policy that says what you do with Boardsesh data, and register its link with your app. Climbers see it before they approve.
items.security: Keep tokens and client secrets on your server or in the device’s secure storage, never in a URL or a log. If you learn that one leaked, or that someone reached climbers’ data without permission, tell us at legal@boardsesh.com within 72 hours.

items.limits: Stay within the rate limits, and wait as long as Retry-After says.
items.scopes: Ask only for the scopes you use. Don’t try to get around a scope, a limit, a suspension or a climber’s choices.
items.catalog: Don’t use the API to copy Boardsesh’s climb catalogue. The public nightly snapshots are there for that.
items.service: Board control, sessions and the climb catalogue are not part of the API. An app whose accounts, climbing, board control or sessions run on Boardsesh’s servers needs our written permission, which we don’t currently give.

items.worksWith: Say that your app works with Boardsesh, for example “Works with Boardsesh” or “Import your Boardsesh logbook”. Don’t suggest that Boardsesh made, reviewed or endorses your app.
items.ownName: Don’t use Boardsesh, or anything that looks like it, in your app’s name, publisher name or icon.
items.boardBrands: Kilter, Tension, MoonBoard and other board names belong to their owners. Use them only to say which board a climb is on, and don’t suggest that a board maker endorses your app or Boardsesh.

items.suspend: Suspend or delete an app that breaks these terms, puts climbers at risk or overloads the service. When we suspend an app, the console shows you the reason.
items.changes: Change the API under the versioning rules in the developer docs, and change these terms. The console shows the new version, and the next app you register accepts it.
items.asIs: The API is provided as it is, with no promise that it is always available or free of errors.

ending.title: Stopping
ending.body: You can delete your app in the console at any time, and every climber’s connection to it ends at once. Then delete the Boardsesh data you hold, unless a climber asked you to keep theirs.

metadata.title: Read a climber's logbook with the Boardsesh API
metadata.description: Register an app, send the climber to approve it, then read their logbook: a full download first, then only what changed. Scopes, limits and errors on one page.

docs.title: Connect an app to a climber's logbook
docs.lead: Let a training planner, a logbook or your own script read a climber's Boardsesh ticks once they approve it. They can disconnect it at any time.

invitation.title: Registration is by invitation
invitation.body: Registration is by invitation while we test it. Each app starts with room for {{live}} climbers connected at once and {{perDay}} new ones per day. To ask for access, email:

open.title: Register your app
open.body: Sign in, verify your developer email and accept the developer terms to create an app in the console. You get a client ID and, if your server exchanges the code, a client secret. No invitation is needed.

items.read: Read every tick the climber has logged, on every board, including ticks they keep private on Boardsesh.
items.sync: Download the whole logbook once, then fetch only what changed. A change usually shows up within a second.
items.profile: Read their display name and avatar, if you ask for that scope.
items.disconnect: The climber can disconnect your app at any time in Settings, Connected apps. Your next call then fails, and you delete what you stored.
items.notYet: Full session and workout sync needs sessions:read. Beta videos and board control are not included.

items.register: Register an app in the developer console and keep the client ID.
items.approve: Send the climber to the authorize URL in their system browser. They sign in and tap Allow.
items.exchange: Swap the code your redirect URI receives for an access token and a refresh token.
items.snapshot: Call the changes endpoint with no cursor and follow every page until hasMore is false. That is the full logbook.
items.feed: From then on, call it with your last cursor to get new, edited and deleted ticks.

scopes.title: Scopes
scopes.lead: Ask for the smallest set you need. The consent screen lists each one in plain words.

items.logbook: Every tick on every board, including ones the climber keeps private.
items.offline: A refresh token, so you can keep reading while the climber is away. It opens no data by itself.
items.sessions: Completed sessions, private recap notes, recorded duration and full workouts, including workouts from other apps. Requires logbook:read.

items.consent: An app without a client secret, and every native app, shows the consent screen on every authorization. prompt=none never returns a code; it returns error=consent_required. Keep the refresh token instead of authorizing again. Only a confidential web app with an https redirect is remembered.
items.redirect: Redirect URIs match as exact strings, up to {{max}} per app. Use https, a loopback address (http://127.0.0.1 or http://[::1], port ignored) or a private-use scheme with a dot in it. http://localhost and wildcards are refused.
items.redirectChange: Adding or replacing a redirect URI asks every climber who approved your app to approve it again. Removing one, or editing the name or links, does not. Tokens you already hold keep working until the climber is asked again.
items.recentSignIn: Adding, replacing or removing a redirect URI, rotating the client secret and deleting an app each need a sign-in within the last {{minutes}} minutes. If yours is older, the console asks you to sign in again.
items.notice: You get an email when redirect URIs change, the secret rotates, an app is deleted or a new app is registered on your account.
items.pkce: PKCE with S256 is required for every app. Send resource=https://api.boardsesh.com/v1 when you authorize, exchange a code and refresh. Tokens issued without it are refused by the API.
items.code: A code lasts {{seconds}} seconds and works once. Sending it twice also ends the tokens it issued, so restart authorization instead of retrying.
items.tokens: An access token lasts 1 hour. A refresh token lasts {{days}} days and changes on every use: store the new one before you use the new access token, and never refresh for one climber in parallel.
items.signin: A climber who last signed in more than 30 days ago, or before their last password change, signs in again before the consent screen.
items.disconnect: If a climber disconnects, resets their password or deletes their account, the API answers 401 invalid_token and a refresh answers invalid_grant. Show a Reconnect Boardsesh state, stop calling for that climber and delete what you stored.

requests.title: A first connection
requests.lead: Open the authorize URL in the system browser, never in an embedded web view. Swap in your own client ID, redirect URI, state and code.
requests.exchange: Your redirect URI gets a code. Exchange it:
requests.sync: Then read the logbook. Leave cursor out the first time and follow the cursor in each answer. Sync when the climber opens your app, and in the background no more than every 15 minutes per climber.
requests.confidential: A confidential app, one that keeps a client secret on its server, also sends client_secret in the body (client_secret_post) or as HTTP Basic (client_secret_basic), whichever it registered. A public app sends only client_id.

items.api: API: {{climber}} requests a minute per climber and {{app}} a minute per app.
items.token: Token endpoint: {{refresh}} refreshes a minute per climber, and {{exchange}} code exchanges or revokes a minute per app per client IP.
items.fullSync: Starting a full download: 2 a minute per climber. A 503 with Retry-After on a download means wait at least that long.
items.page: limit runs from 1 to 200 and defaults to 100. A page can be empty and still have hasMore: true.
items.history: Changes are kept for 90 days. An older cursor answers 410 cursor_expired; start a full download without a cursor.
items.body: A request body over 64 KB answers 413.
items.caps: Early access: {{apps}} apps per developer account, and per app {{live}} climbers connected at once and {{perDay}} new ones in 24 hours.
items.headers: Every response carries Boardsesh-Request-Id and RateLimit headers. A 429 carries Retry-After in seconds.

errors.title: Errors
errors.lead: Errors are JSON with error, message and requestId. Branch on the HTTP status first; new codes can appear.

items.invalidToken: The access token expired or was revoked. Refresh once and retry. If the refresh fails, ask the climber to reconnect.
items.insufficientScope: The token doesn't carry the scope this call needs.
items.cursorExpired: The cursor is too old or no longer valid. Start a full download without a cursor.
items.rateLimited: Over a limit. Wait for the seconds in Retry-After.
items.busy: Boardsesh is busy or paused app access for a moment. Wait for Retry-After and retry. It never means the climber disconnected.

versioning.title: Versions
versioning.body: The version is in the path, /v1. New fields, routes, scopes and enum values arrive on v1 without notice, so read what you know and ignore the rest. Removing or renaming a field becomes v2, and v1 keeps running for at least six months with a Sunset header on every response.

auth.title: Connect a climber with OAuth
auth.description: Register an app, authorize with PKCE and keep rotating credentials safe.

registration.title: Register your app
registration.body:
Sign in at /developers/apps and verify your email for developer access. Register a public native app for a command-line tool, mobile app or desktop app; register a public web app for a browser, or a confidential app when your server exchanges the code. Keep the secret on that server.

Register the exact redirect URI. A native app may use http://127.0.0.1:8765/oauth/boardsesh or http://[::1]:8765/oauth/boardsesh; the loopback port is ignored when matching. https URLs and private-use schemes with a dot are allowed. localhost, wildcards, fragments, Boardsesh hosts and Boardsesh schemes are refused. Each account can register 10 apps, with 10 redirects per app. Default connection limits are 25 active climbers and 20 new connections in any 24 hours. Ask support@boardsesh.com about higher limits.

authorize.title: Authorize in the system browser
authorize.body:
Discover endpoints from https://api.boardsesh.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server/api/auth. The issuer is https://api.boardsesh.com/api/auth and the resource is exactly https://api.boardsesh.com/v1. Send that resource when authorizing, exchanging and refreshing.

Generate a random PKCE verifier and S256 challenge, plus at least 128 random bits for state. Ask for logbook:read and offline_access; add profile:read only for the name and avatar. Open the authorize URL in a system browser. On return, verify state and iss before exchanging the code. Codes last 60 seconds and work once. Restart authorization if an exchange has an uncertain outcome.

credentials.title: Store each rotated token before using it
credentials.body:
Access tokens last one hour and refresh tokens 90 days. Every refresh replaces the refresh token. Serialize refreshes for a climber and durably store the new pair before using the access token. Replaying a consumed refresh token invalidates its family. Never retry a refresh after a network failure whose outcome is unknown; reconnect instead.

A 401 means refresh once and retry. invalid_grant means reconnect, then stop calling with that credential. Keep the authentication method registered by the app: none, client_secret_post or client_secret_basic. Browser clients use registered https redirect origins for CORS; do not store credentials in browser preferences.

disconnect.title: Disconnect the whole connection
disconnect.body: DELETE /v1/connection needs no extra scope. A 204 confirms disconnect; remove stored credentials and the climber’s copy unless they asked you to keep it. A 401 alone does not prove an earlier DELETE succeeded. Refresh once and retry; if credentials are unusable, ask the climber to check Connected apps in Boardsesh. Revoking one token through the OAuth revoke endpoint does not disconnect every credential family. Password changes and account deletion also disconnect apps.

sync.title: Keep a complete logbook in sync
sync.description: Download a full snapshot, commit changes and cursors together, and recover safely after expiry.

snapshot.title: Build a replacement copy first
snapshot.body:
GET /v1/logbook/changes with no cursor starts a complete snapshot, including unchanged old ticks and ticks from before this API existed. Follow every cursor until hasMore is false; the last snapshot page enters incremental catch-up and still has hasMore: true. Empty pages may also have hasMore: true. limit defaults to 100 and ranges from 1 to 200.

Build a separate replacement copy. Publish it and its final cursor in one durable transaction, keeping the previous copy until then. After a crash during bootstrap, discard the abandoned replacement and restart without a cursor. Never apply snapshot pages as incremental changes to your previous live copy.

changes.title: Apply each page and cursor together
changes.body:
With logbook:read, upsert tick entries by tick.id and remove tick.deleted entries by id, even if you never saw that tick. Apply entries in order, ignore unknown change types and retain fields you do not yet understand. Persist the page’s mutations and cursor atomically, and serialize sync for each climber.

A tick carries the climber’s own attempts, grade, stars and comment. Catalog grades may change without a tick change. Never infer a deletion from an empty incremental page. The account ID from GET /v1/me is stable for your app across reconnects and different for other apps; keep copies isolated by app and account.

recovery.title: Recover from 410 without losing the previous copy
recovery.body:
A 410 cursor_expired requires a complete replacement, never just resetting the cursor against your old copy. Persist a full-sync-required marker before the next request. Snapshot cursors expire after one hour and belong to one app connection. Incremental retention is controlled by the pruning watermark; do not expire a cursor using its age alone.

The example client keeps credentials, ticks, the cursor and the full-sync marker in one private JSON file. It holds an exclusive lock for the command, writes replacements with atomic rename, serializes refreshes and retries network errors, 429 and 5xx with backoff. If a command crashes, confirm it has stopped before removing its leftover .lock file.

poll.title: Poll when the climber needs it
poll.body:
Sync when the climber opens your app. Background sync runs no more than once every 15 minutes per climber. Honor Retry-After on 429 and temporary 503 responses. Optional logbook.changed webhooks tell you to run this same sync; they do not replace the feed.

Keep all private ticks private in your app too. A tick on someone else’s non-public Spraywall redacts the climb name and Spraywall identity. Do not build a climb catalog or publish other setters’ draft or unlisted climbs from a logbook.

sessions.title: Sync completed sessions and workouts
sessions.body:
Ask for logbook:read sessions:read offline_access to import completed personal, inferred and joined shared sessions. Active sessions and permanent gym sessions are excluded. Session records include the recap, stored start/end times, durationSeconds and the climber’s full workout plan and results, including workouts supplied by other apps. Missing or reversed recorded times give a null duration; never estimate from ticks. Another creator’s private recap and labels are withheld. Beta links and hold positions are excluded.

Upsert session entries by session.id, remove session.deleted entries by id, and use tick.sessionId to group climbs. References can arrive on different pages. GET /v1/logbook/sessions/{id} reads one eligible session. Keep both entity types in the same replacement copy and commit them with their cursor.

Existing tick-only tokens do not gain this access. Request fresh consent with sessions:read, replace the stored token pair, and start a complete replacement import without the old cursor. A cursor from the earlier access level returns 410. The replacement includes older sessions from before the integration; missing historical workout plans or timestamps cannot be reconstructed.

attribution.title: Credit Boardsesh and link back to the session
attribution.body:
Every imported session’s primary view must visibly credit Boardsesh. “Boardsesh” or “Recorded with Boardsesh” in a small footer or footnote is sufficient. A credit hidden inside an ellipsis menu is not sufficient.

We also recommend an “Open in Boardsesh” action using the session’s url or appUrl. The action may live in an ellipsis menu and need not be primary. History links require the climber to sign in with an account that recorded or joined the session; they open read-only detail and never join a session. Keep the HTTPS fallback usable without the app.

errors.title: Handle API failures and limits
errors.description: Know when to refresh, rebuild a logbook, wait or ask the climber to reconnect.

status.title: Branch on HTTP status first
status.body:
400 means a malformed request or cursor. 401 invalid_token means refresh once and retry; invalid_grant during refresh means reconnect. 403 insufficient_scope needs authorization for that scope. 404 hides resources owned by another app or climber. 409 means a conflict, including a reused externalRef or cancelling a started workout. 410 cursor_expired means a full replacement sync. 413 means a body larger than 64 KB; 422 means validation or idempotency mismatch.

429 and 5xx are retryable. Honor Retry-After and use bounded exponential backoff. Network failures do not prove revocation. Error codes and fields can grow on v1, so tolerate new ones. Errors carry error, message and requestId; validation errors may add field. OAuth uses error and error_description.

limits.title: Read the response headers
limits.body:
API calls allow 120 requests per minute per app/climber and 6,000 per app. Refresh allows 10 per minute per connection. Code exchange and revoke allow 60 per minute per app/client IP. A new app allows 25 active climbers and 20 new connections per rolling 24 hours. An administrator may adjust an app’s connection caps.

RateLimit-Limit, RateLimit-Remaining and RateLimit-Reset describe the tightest request limit; Retry-After gives the wait in seconds. Boardsesh-Request-Id identifies the request in support logs. Never send access tokens, refresh tokens, codes or client secrets to support.

versions.title: Expect additive changes
versions.body:
v1 can add fields, routes, scopes, event types and enum values. Ignore what you do not understand. Removing or renaming a field requires v2; v1 continues for at least six months with a Sunset header. Every contract change is listed in the developer changelog.

Use the OpenAPI 3.1 document to generate a client or mock the API offline. The mock demonstrates response shapes, not OAuth security or real cursor semantics. Test authorization and synchronization against your own account before shipping.

reference.title: Boardsesh partner API reference
reference.description: Explore the scoped REST API and download its OpenAPI 3.1 contract.

contract.title: Use the published contract
contract.body:
The API host is https://api.boardsesh.com. Calls under /v1 use an opaque Bearer token for the resource https://api.boardsesh.com/v1. OAuth endpoints and their metadata are separate from this REST contract. The reference below uses the same committed OpenAPI document as the backend.

Generate a client from the document or run the Prism mock below. Every response example is illustrative. The mock cannot authorize an app, refresh a token, maintain a snapshot or enforce ownership. Use your own account for those flows.

changelog.title: Boardsesh API changelog
changelog.description: Read the changes to the versioned API contract, newest first.

contract.title: Contract changes
contract.body: Entries come from the same committed changelog checked against the generated OpenAPI document in CI. New fields and routes remain on v1; removals and renames require a new major version. Check this page when updating your client.

webhooks.title: Webhooks for {{app}}
webhooks.description: Receive a notification when a logbook changes, a workout finishes or a connection ends. Notifications contain no climbing data.
webhooks.failed: Webhook settings could not be saved or loaded. Try again.
webhooks.urlHelp: Public HTTPS on port 443. Private addresses and redirects are refused.
webhooks.testQueued: Test delivery queued. Refresh the delivery list to see its result.
webhooks.secretOnce: Copy this secret now. It will not be shown again.
webhooks.rotationHelp: After rotation, requests carry signatures from both secrets for 24 hours. Update your receiver before the old secret expires.
webhooks.endpointGone: This endpoint returned HTTP 410. Fix the endpoint, then re-enable deliveries.
webhooks.failuresDisabled: Deliveries were disabled after repeated failures. Fix the endpoint, then re-enable them.
webhooks.reauthBody: Changing webhook settings or rotating its secret requires a sign-in within the last {{minutes}} minutes. Sign in again to protect where notifications are delivered.
webhooks.reauthForm: Signing in again leaves this page and clears unsaved webhook edits. Copy your endpoint URL before continuing.

gymMcp.title: Manage your gyms with an AI assistant
gymMcp.lead: Connect ChatGPT or Claude to Boardsesh to check gym activity and manage your gym from a conversation.
gymMcp.availability: Access is rolling out in stages. If connecting is unavailable for your account, keep using Manage gym and try again after you receive access.

setup.title: Connect your assistant
setup.copyFailed: Copy did not work. Select the URL above and copy it.

steps.add: In ChatGPT plugins or Claude connectors, add a custom remote MCP server.
steps.paste: Paste the server URL. Choose OAuth and the published client identity option.
steps.signIn: Sign in to Boardsesh and review the gym permissions before allowing access.
steps.try: Open a conversation with the connector and ask which gyms you can manage.

setup.requirements: You do not install anything or register a developer app. Your assistant account and workspace must allow custom MCP connections. Available settings and plans vary by provider.

access.title: What your assistant can do
access.gyms: One connection covers all gyms your Boardsesh account can manage, including gyms you gain access to later. Your current role limits every action.
access.actions: Read activity reports, edit gym details and branding, manage boards and TVs, reply to comments, and manage eligible staff access.
access.approvals: Review write requests before approving them in your assistant. The assistant controls when approval appears; Boardsesh checks your current permissions for every operation.
access.privacy: Tool results are shared with the assistant you choose. Your Boardsesh password is entered only on the Boardsesh sign-in page.

examples.title: Try a request
examples.activity: “Show the last 30 days of activity at my gym, including coverage limits.”
examples.tv: “Create a TV display with our Kilter and Tension boards.”
examples.profile: “Update our gym description to say we open at 8 on Saturdays.”
examples.photos: For a photo or logo, provide a public HTTPS image URL. You can also upload a file from the gym’s profile or branding tab.

disconnect.title: Stop assistant access
disconnect.body: Open Settings, find the assistant in Connected apps, and choose Disconnect. Future requests stop working. Information already shared remains with the assistant.

gymMcp.pilotAvailability: This connector is in an invitation-only pilot. Only invited Boardsesh accounts can connect. Wait for your invitation before following the sign-in steps below.
